subject: Creativity
title: IDEO's Shopping Cart: Design Thinking in 5 Days
description: One-minute skill: IDEO's Shopping Cart: Design Thinking in 5 Days.

hook.text: In 1999, ABC Nightline challenged IDEO to redesign the shopping cart in five days.

buildup.text: IDEO's team spent day one ONLY observing — watching shoppers, interviewing store workers, studying pain points.

discovery.text: They found the real problems: child safety, theft, navigation in crowded aisles — issues no engineer would identify.

twist.text: The final design was modular — removable baskets, better turning radius, child seats. Not futuristic-looking.

climax.text: The episode became the most-referenced design thinking case study in business schools worldwide — watched by millions.

punchline.text: Five days. One shopping cart. A permanent change in how the world thinks about.

quiz.question: What did IDEO spend the first day of the shopping cart challenge doing?
options: Only observing shoppers and interviewing store workers

details.summary: In 1999, design firm IDEO redesigned a shopping cart in five days on camera for ABC's Nightline. The episode showed design thinking in action: user observation, brainstorming, rapid prototyping, and testing, making design thinking visible and accessible to a mainstream audience.
details.whyItMatters: The IDEO shopping cart project became the most famous demonstration of design thinking in practice. It proved that the process could be applied to any product and executed at speed.
takeaways: IDEO redesigned a shopping cart in five days on national television
The process demonstrated user research, ideation, and prototyping live
The episode made design thinking accessible to business audiences

faq.question: What innovations came out of the shopping cart redesign?
faq.answer: The team introduced modular, nestable baskets, child safety features, improved wheel design, and a scanning-friendly layout. More importantly, the innovations came from observing real shoppers rather than from engineering specifications.

faq.question: Is the IDEO approach still relevant?
faq.answer: The core principles of observing users, brainstorming without judgment, and rapidly prototyping remain foundational. While specific methods have evolved, the human-centered philosophy IDEO demonstrated continues to drive modern design practice.
